question: Does the Arch package install and work on a clean Arch machine that is not the one it was developed on -- the last declared family whose package has only ever been installed by its author?
why_now: M6 line 321 asks for the clean-system checks on each declared family, and line 325 for a fresh installation through sign-in and reboot on each. Ubuntu and Fedora both have them. Arch has neither, and it is the family the project is developed on, which makes it the one most likely to work by accident: the development machine has every build dependency, a configured desktop, and a developer install that the package would have to coexist with. Shipping a 1.0 whose own distribution's package had never been installed anywhere else would be the wrong way round.
how: A third VM, Arch installed unattended from the 2026.09.01 image. archiso has no kickstart and no autoinstall; its `script=` boot parameter is the hook that makes this possible at all. GNOME and gdm with autologin, so there is a session to sign in from. Deliberately absent: fuse3, python-nautilus and the GNOME appindicator extension -- the same rule the Fedora kickstart now follows, so that installing the package is what has to bring them.

predictions.P1: The unattended install completes. The likeliest failure is the `script=` hook itself, which is less travelled than a kickstart or an autoinstall file, and the second likeliest is GRUB on GPT without a BIOS boot partition -- which is why there is one.
predictions.P2: pacman installs both packages from the CI-built archives, pulling fuse3 as a dependency of cirrove and gtk4/libadwaita as dependencies of cirrove-desktop. The Arch packaging has never had its dependencies tested against a machine that lacked them.
predictions.P3: The user unit, the autostart entry, the icons, the metainfo, the Files extension and now the translation catalogues all land where the other two families put them, and `cirrove --help` runs.
predictions.P4: After a reboot the tray starts from the packaged autostart entry and the service is active, with no account -- the same honest empty state the other two showed.
predictions.P5: Removal with pacman leaves nothing named cirrove under /usr or /etc.
predictions.P6: The German catalogue installs and the window is German when the session is, which has only ever been seen from a developer install.

run.where: A third VM, Arch 2026.09.01 installed unattended in 88 seconds -- 533 packages, GNOME and gdm with autologin -- and the packages CI built for the current tree, 0.1.0dev.r428.g94e5e41.

observed.P1: HOLDS. The archiso `script=` hook ran the installer at boot and the machine powered itself off with CIRROVE-ARCH-INSTALL-COMPLETE in the serial log. GRUB on GPT found its BIOS boot partition and reported no error. It came up with gdm active and tester logged in on seat0 without a hand on it.
observed.P2: WRONG, and this is the finding. Arch does not install the desktop integration at all. nautilus-python and gnome-shell-extension-appindicator are optdepends in the PKGBUILD, and pacman does not install optional dependencies -- that is the distribution's convention, not a mistake in the packaging. So where Fedora's Recommends and Debian's Recommends both bring them in by default, an Arch user gets a working mount with no Files badges and no tray icon on GNOME, and only a line in pacman's output to say so. The names are right: Arch calls it nautilus-python, which is what the PKGBUILD says. fuse3, gtk4 and libadwaita were already present because the GNOME stack pulls them, exactly as on Fedora, so the hard dependencies cannot be shown absent on a desktop machine either.
observed.P3: HOLDS. Every file where the other two families put it, including the German catalogue at /usr/share/locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/cirrove.mo and seven icons, and `cirrove --version` runs.
observed.P4: HOLDS. After a reboot with nothing started by hand, cirroved.service is active and cirrove-tray is running from the packaged /etc/xdg/autostart entry. The item is Passive because there is no account, and the journal carries Cirrove's own explanation: no tray host is running, GNOME needs an AppIndicator extension.
observed.P5: HOLDS. pacman -Rns left nothing named cirrove under /usr or /etc, and left ~/.local/state/cirrove alone.
observed.P6: HOLDS. With the session in German the packaged window is German -- Ihre Clouds, in Dateien; Cloud-Laufwerke; OneDrive-Anleitung; the footer -- which had only ever been seen from a developer install.

run.also_found: Looking at that German window found three strings that were never marked for translation, and then a real defect behind two of them. The tray-missing banner and the restart banner were written across two lines with a `\` continuation. Rust strips the newline and the following indentation; xgettext reads the file as C and keeps it. So the extracted message ids carried eighteen spaces in the middle and could never match what the running program looks up -- the entries would have sat in the catalogue, translated, and never appeared. Nothing would have reported it: the tests passed and the catalogue was complete. Both strings are now on one line and scripts/test-translations.py refuses a message id containing a run of spaces.
run.not_covered: Sign-in, and therefore a mount, on Arch. The owner is not at this keyboard and a second copy of a real credential is not worth a test; the mount, its behaviour under a policy and the desktop surfaces with an account are all evidenced on Fedora.

conclusion: The last declared family now has its clean-machine installation. Arch installs, runs, comes back after a reboot from the packaged autostart alone, speaks German from the package, and removes without a trace. One prediction was wrong in a way worth keeping: Arch's optdepends mean the Files badges and the GNOME tray arrive on Fedora and Ubuntu and do not arrive on Arch. That is the distribution's convention rather than a packaging error, so it belongs in the user guide rather than in a Depends line -- and the window already says so on its own, which this run showed it doing. Sign-in on Arch stays open and is the only thing between this and the row.
